title: Beginning smaller
statement: Dependence is a starting condition, not a verdict on worth.
explanation: Adler saw the child's helplessness among more capable people as a common beginning of inferiority feelings. These feelings can prompt learning and striving; they do not automatically constitute a disorder.
nuance:
A child cannot yet reach, read or decide what adults can. The experience of not yet being able helps organize a movement toward greater competence. Adler asks what direction that movement takes, especially whether it develops with an interest in others.

His theory should not be read as saying that everyone has one secret defect explaining their whole life. A feeling of being less capable is different from actually being less valuable. The response to the feeling, and the social setting around it, are central.
metaphor: A small figure meets a series of uneven steps; the higher position is shown as a possibility of learning.

composition.description: A small figure meets a series of uneven steps; the higher position is shown as a possibility of learning.

title: An answer to difficulty
statement: A limitation does not dictate the single life that follows it.
explanation: Adler's account of compensation concerns efforts to respond to experienced insufficiency. A difficulty can encourage new skills or become the center of a defensive struggle for status.
nuance:
Someone struggling with one activity may practice intensely or find another way of contributing. Adler's early interest in bodily limitations developed into a wider account of psychological and social responses.

Compensation is not the claim that every hardship is secretly a gift. Difficulties can remain painful and opportunities are unequal. What interests Adler is how the person interprets the difficulty and organizes a response, rather than treating one bodily or social condition as an unchangeable destiny.
metaphor: One obstacle branches into different possible routes rather than a single predetermined outcome.

composition.description: One obstacle branches into different possible routes rather than a single predetermined outcome.

title: When less becomes a life
statement: The problem grows when felt inadequacy rules the whole field of action.
explanation: For Adler, an intensified and unresolved sense of inferiority can discourage participation. Instead of treating a difficulty as something to meet, the person organizes life around avoiding exposure to it.
nuance:
A person who assumes any mistake will prove they are worthless may stop attempting tasks they could learn. The complex is not simply modesty or awareness of a skill gap. It concerns the organizing force of the judgment.

Adler asks about the person's goal and relation to others as well as the feeling itself. Removing one obstacle may not help if a demand for complete security still makes every uncertain activity unacceptable. The distinction is between not yet succeeding and treating possible failure as a verdict on existence.
metaphor: A figure retreats from an available test while the imagined measuring line keeps rising.

composition.description: A figure retreats from an available test while the imagined measuring line keeps rising.

title: Toward more
statement: The question is what becoming more capable is for.
explanation: Adler described a movement from felt insufficiency toward greater security, completion or superiority. Its direction matters: developing a capacity with others differs from needing to stand above them.
nuance:
Two people may pursue the same skill. One wants to do useful work; the other wants proof that no one can rival them. Outward achievement alone does not show which aim organizes the effort.

Striving for superiority in Adler's terminology is not always simple domination. His writing distinguishes growth and adaptation from a personal goal of power over others. Reading the phrase only as competitive ambition misses the contrast at the center of his account.
metaphor: A route toward an imagined destination is set beside a shared crossing, asking whether the goal connects or separates.

composition.description: A route toward an imagined destination is set beside a shared crossing, asking whether the goal connects or separates.

title: The elevated position
statement: Looking superior can be a way to avoid feeling inferior.
explanation: Adler interpreted some displays of dominance or importance as answers to threatened self-worth. Being above others promises security while keeping attention fixed on personal rank.
nuance:
Someone who must win every discussion may be protecting a fragile sense of competence rather than expressing stable confidence. That is an interpretive possibility, not a diagnosis that follows from assertiveness alone.

The display can also make cooperation more difficult, preserving the insecurity it tries to escape. Adler's concern is the whole pattern: the imagined danger, the compensating goal and the social effect. Humiliation by others does not become justified because a person has adopted an unhelpful defense.
metaphor: A figure rises on a short pedestal while the neighboring figures remain disconnected from it.

composition.description: A figure rises on a short pedestal while the neighboring figures remain disconnected from it.

title: Room for an imperfect attempt
statement: Participation asks for courage before it offers certainty.
explanation: Adler associated discouragement with withdrawal from life's demands. In his account, courage allows a person to meet a task without first securing an invulnerable image of themselves.
nuance:
A learner who can make a visible error has more room to learn than one who must never appear inexperienced. Courage here is not dramatic fearlessness. It is willingness to take part despite an uncertain result.

The social setting matters: ridicule and impossible demands can make participation harder. Adler's educational emphasis therefore includes how people encourage one another. Telling someone to be brave is a thin substitute for a relationship in which an imperfect attempt is allowed.
metaphor: An uneven bridge develops between two figures instead of requiring one figure to leap the empty gap alone.

composition.description: An uneven bridge develops between two figures instead of requiring one figure to leap the empty gap alone.
